question: Should OpenClaw make `message_sending` a universal pre-send policy boundary across all outbound paths, and should hook failure block delivery by default?
rationale: The remaining work changes public plugin-hook guarantees, cross-channel delivery ownership, and security-sensitive failure behavior, so an automated repair should not choose those semantics without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design the universal boundary
options.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella, define the hook/failure contract, and land a cross-channel implementation with upgrade notes and tests.

options.title: Continue narrow channel repairs
options.body: Track each missing channel or tool path separately while avoiding a global security guarantee until semantics are settled.

options.title: Document best-effort behavior
options.body: Decline the unbypassable guarantee and document `message_sending` as useful but not security-grade enforcement.

recommendation.title: Design the universal boundary
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella, define the hook/failure contract, and land a cross-channel implementation with upgrade notes and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history across the sampled outbound, reply-dispatch, plugin SDK, Signal, and Telegram boundary files.
